notes: One run per config per eval (n=1), so no variance estimate. Treat the differences as qualitative.
Tokens are total processed tokens from the subagent transcript, cache reads included, so they mostly track how many turns a run took.

test-file-move: only the lean skill executed the real move; old_skill and without_skill ran the same decision as a dry run, because the brief allows a single real move of one test file. N/A rows are excluded from pass rates.

'discriminating' marks assertions whose verdicts differ between configs. Non-discriminating ones are kept as safety regression checks rather than removed, and the discriminating pass rate is reported separately.
The lean report-only run took longer and processed more tokens than old_skill because it read two reference files and ran build_report.py (15 tool calls vs 10).

skill_md_size.estimate: tokens ~ chars/4: old ~8.3k loaded on every trigger; lean ~3.2k on trigger, plus ~0.5-1k per reference read when needed
